<subagent sessionID="ses_e5cb03069ffeRjpyR4ZhUZWgeg" state="completed">
## Repository findings

- **Framework:** No application framework is set up yet. The repository has no root `package.json`, `index.html`, or app source; it is currently a project shell rather than an existing game.
- **Entry points:** There is no game entry point. The startup scripts are `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/start.sh` and `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/capture.sh`. `start.sh` delegates to the OMGithub runtime, and `capture.sh` delegates to its browser-capture script.
- **Existing game code/assets:** None found in the project. The `.agents/skills` directory contains tooling and sample viewer files, but no project game code or game assets.
- **How it runs:** `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/start.sh` expects `RUNTIME_DIR` and launches the runtime’s default server. That server supports either a root `index.html` or a Vite project; for Vite it installs dependencies, builds to `dist`, and serves on port 3000 by default. In this environment, the runtime directory is `/home/runner/work/_temp/omgithub-runtime`. As checked out, startup will fail because the project has neither a supported Vite package nor an `index.html`. The capture script expects `CAPTURE_URL` and `CAPTURE_DIR`.

## Recommended implementation plan

1. **Bootstrap a small Vite + Three.js app**—a good fit for a 3D FPS and compatible with the provided launcher. Use `index.html` and `src/main.js` as the entry points; keep UI styling and game systems in separate source files.
2. **Build one polished, focused arena** with a strong visual identity: a compact, readable environment, atmospheric lighting/fog, and clear landmarks. Start with procedural or lightweight geometry and generated materials rather than assuming any existing assets.
3. **Implement a complete playable loop:** title/start state, first-person movement and aiming, shooting with hit feedback, zombies that approach and attack, health/ammo/reload, escalating waves, and game-over/restart. Separate input, player, zombie, weapon, HUD, and wave logic so tuning stays manageable.
4. **Make touch a first-class control scheme:** left-side movement joystick, right-side drag-to-look, and prominent fire/reload buttons. Add desktop WASD/mouse controls, respect mobile safe areas, prevent unwanted browser gestures during play, and make HUD and buttons scale to small screens.
5. **Prioritize mobile performance:** cap pixel ratio, use lightweight geometry/materials and limited dynamic lights, reuse enemy instances where practical, and keep effects short and restrained. Provide a visible loading/start state and handle resize/orientation changes.
6. **Verify the actual launch and captures:** after adding the app, run `RUNTIME_DIR=/home/runner/work/_temp/omgithub-runtime ./start.sh`, confirm it responds on port 3000, then use `capture.sh` with `CAPTURE_URL` and `CAPTURE_DIR` set to inspect desktop and mobile renders.

Useful repository references: `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/README.md` is only project-hosting boilerplate; `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/Agents.md` documents the browser-capture expectations.
</subagent>

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable, realistic-looking, high-detail, mobile-friendly FPS zombie shooter with good graphics and animations.

## Requirements
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.
- Finish the game build and note assumptions briefly when reporting completion.

## Decisions
- Use Vite and Three.js with a procedural 3D quarantine-zone arena, first-person rifle, zombie waves, combat HUD, and touch controls.
- Target both desktop keyboard/mouse and mobile joystick, drag-to-aim, fire, and reload controls.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created the Vite app, game UI, procedural 3D environment, weapon and zombie models, combat loop, HUD, and mobile/desktop inputs.
- `npm install` and `npm run build` succeeded.
- Captured and inspected `screenshots/title.png` and `screenshots/game.png`; found the scene too dark, the rifle missing, and wave spawning broken.
- Brightened the scene, added the camera to the scene so attached weapon geometry renders, and replaced the blank quarantine sign with generated text.
- Reworked wave state to use `spawnRemaining` and `spawnDelay`, fixing the premature wave-advance behavior.

### Active
- Validate the latest changes in-browser and verify gameplay, zombie spawning, rifle rendering, mobile layout, and build.
- The dev server was restarted and served successfully at `http://localhost:5173`.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run `npm run build`.
2. Reload the browser at `http://localhost:5173`, deploy, and inspect gameplay plus console errors.
3. Fix any remaining visual/gameplay bugs; capture a mobile view if possible.
4. Summarize the completed game and testing, including assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game screens and HUD markup.
- `src/main.js`: Three.js scene, gameplay systems, controls, and waves.
- `src/style.css`: Visual design and responsive/mobile styling.
- `package.json`: Vite scripts and dependencies.
- `screenshots/title.png`: Previous title-screen capture.
- `screenshots/game.png`: Previous gameplay capture before the recent fixes.

## Important Context
- Latest wave logic uses `spawnRemaining` and `spawnDelay`; verify that waves advance only after all hostiles are defeated.
- The earlier screenshot showed an absent rifle; `scene.add(camera)` was added to render camera-attached weapon geometry, but this has not yet been rechecked.
- Browser capture via `playwright-cli` required installing Chromium; it is now installed.
- Changes are uncommitted.
